text:
Predicates:
Barks(x) ::: x barks
Dog(x) ::: x is a dog
Animal(x) ::: x is an animal
Jump(x) ::: x jumps
HasLegs(x) ::: x has legs
Terricolous(x) ::: x is terricolous
KiKi ::: KiKi
Likes(x, y) ::: x likes y

Premises:
∀x (Barks(x) → Dog(x)) ::: All dogs bark.
∀x (Dog(x) → Barks(x)) ::: All dogs are animals that bark.
∀x (Jump(x) → Animal(x)) ::: All animals that jump.
∀x (HasLegs(x) → Jump(x)) ::: Animals with legs jump.
∀x (Terricolous(x) → HasLegs(x)) ::: Terricolous animals have legs.
Animal(KiKi) ::: KiKi is an animal.
(¬Jump(KiKi) ∧ ¬HasLegs(KiKi)) → (Terricolous(KiKi) ∨ HasLegs(KiKi)) ::: If KiKi neither jumps nor has legs, then KiKi is terricolous or has legs.

Conclusion:
¬Barks(KiKi) ∧ ¬Dog(KiKi) ::: KiKi does not bark and he is not a dog
